title: System Network
description: Choose which destinations the operating system sends through Yuhaiin TUNs or other interfaces, and let other devices use this host as their gateway.

stateHelp.degraded: Partly applied. Earlier routes may still be in use.
stateHelp.conflict: Some destinations are already routed by another program; its routes keep priority.
stateHelp.unavailable: The target interface or TUN does not exist right now. Routes come back automatically when it returns.
stateHelp.unsupported: This device cannot apply this rule.
stateHelp.failed: Could not be applied. The previous working routes are kept.

savedWithProblems: Saved. Some rules could not be applied; see their status.
unsaved: Unsaved changes. The operating system still uses the last applied rules.
invalid: Fix the highlighted rules before saving.

platform.linux: Linux: rules use a dedicated policy-routing table owned by Yuhaiin. Interfaces of other programs are never changed.
platform.darwin: macOS: rules are added to the system routing table. There is no policy routing, so a destination that another program already routes keeps that route and is shown as a conflict.
platform.windows: Windows: rules are added to the system routing table per interface. Policy routing is not available.
platform.android: Android: rules decide which destinations the Yuhaiin VPN captures. Other interfaces and forwarding are not available. Without rules, the route profile chosen in the app applies.
platform.none: This device cannot manage system routes.

routing.title: Route rules
routing.help: Rules are checked from top to bottom. The first rule that matches a destination wins, so put specific rules above broad ones.
routing.emptyHelp: Without rules, Yuhaiin does not change where the operating system sends traffic. Add a rule to send, for example, all internet traffic through a Yuhaiin TUN, or one network through WireGuard.
routing.overriddenBy: Some destinations are already taken by: {{names}}
routing.shadowed: Every destination is already taken by rules above it ({{names}}), so this rule has no effect.
routing.stale: Using the routes from the last successful update.
routing.requiredHelp: Routes a running TUN needs to work, such as its FakeIP pool. They are installed before any rule.
routing.migrationHelp: Route settings that used to be part of TUN inbounds now live here. Review the rules below.

editor.name: Name
editor.targetTunHelp: A TUN created by one of your Yuhaiin inbounds.
editor.targetInterfaceHelp: WireGuard, Tailscale, another VPN, Ethernet or Wi-Fi.
editor.noTuns: No TUN inbound exists yet. Create one in Inbounds first.
editor.interfaceNotFound: {{name}} is not present right now. The rule waits until it appears.
editor.gatewayHelp: Ethernet and Wi-Fi need a router address. Leave empty to use the detected one.
editor.gatewayNone: None detected: enter the router address of this network.
editor.gatewayNotNeeded: Point-to-point interfaces such as VPNs need no gateway.
editor.priorityHelp: Lower numbers are checked first. You can also use the arrows in the list.

error.empty: Add at least one network or country, or turn on reverse selection.

global.title: Global
global.example: Example: websites, games and apps all use this route. Local-only traffic such as multicast and link-local stays on your network.

non_private.title: Non-private
non_private.description: Internet traffic, except private networks and LAN traffic.
non_private.example: Example: google.com uses this route, while your router (192.168.1.1), a NAS and Tailscale devices (100.x.x.x) are reached directly.

custom.title: Custom
custom.description: Only the networks or countries you choose.
custom.example: Example: only 10.0.0.0/8 and addresses in Japan (JP).

defaults.title: Private networks are excluded automatically
defaults.help: LAN devices, Tailscale (100.64.0.0/10 and its fd7a:115c:a1e0::/48 IPv6 range) and other private addresses are not routed. You normally do not need to change this.
defaults.private: Private, shared (CGNAT / Tailscale) and unique local IPv6

include.label: Also include
include.help: Private networks that should still use this rule, one per line. Example: 10.8.0.0/16 for an office network you can only reach through this target.

bypass.label: Bypass
bypass.helpGlobal: Networks that keep using your normal network, one per line. Example: 192.168.1.0/24 to reach your LAN directly.
bypass.helpNonPrivate: Networks that keep using your normal network, one per line. If you reach a network through a Tailscale subnet router, add it here: advertised subnets are not always private addresses (for example 203.0.113.0/24).
bypass.helpCustom: Addresses inside the networks or countries above that keep using your normal network.

match.priority: If a network is in both lists, bypass wins.

custom.cidrHelp: One IPv4 or IPv6 network per line. A single address such as 8.8.8.8 is also accepted.
custom.countriesHelp: Uses the GeoIP database set in Routing lists. Routes update automatically when the database is refreshed; while it is missing, the last routes stay in place.
custom.invertLabel: All countries except the selected ones
custom.invertOff: Off: only the selected countries use this rule.
custom.invertOn: On: everything except the selected countries uses this rule. Private networks still stay on your network.
custom.invertWithoutCountries: No country is selected, so all internet traffic uses this rule.

cidr.cidr: Line {{line}}: "{{value}}" is not a valid IP address or CIDR.
cidr.prefix: Line {{line}}: "{{value}}" has an invalid prefix length (IPv4 0–32, IPv6 0–128).
cidr.zone: Line {{line}}: "{{value}}" contains an interface zone, which routes cannot use.

forwarding.unsupported: Forwarding is not available on this device.
forwarding.introTitle: Use this host as a side router
forwarding.introHelp: Forwarding lets other devices on your LAN send their traffic through this host, for example into a Yuhaiin TUN.
forwarding.step1: On the LAN device (or your DHCP server), set the gateway to this host's LAN address.
forwarding.step2: Turn on IPv4 forwarding below and add a rule for the LAN devices.
forwarding.step3: Turn on NAT only if the next router has no route back to your LAN.
forwarding.ipv4Help: Turns on net.ipv4.ip_forward. Yuhaiin restores the previous value when it stops, unless another service changed it meanwhile.
forwarding.ipv6Help: Turns on net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding. Note: Linux then ignores router advertisements, so a host that gets its IPv6 default route that way may lose it.
forwarding.empty: No forwarding rules. Without a rule, traffic from other devices is not sent to a Yuhaiin target.
forwarding.offNote: Rules are inactive while forwarding is off for their IP version.
forwarding.ingressHelp: The interface the LAN devices are connected to.
forwarding.sourcesHelp: Addresses of the devices to forward, one per line. Example: 192.168.20.0/24 for the whole LAN, or 192.168.20.50 for one device. Leave empty to forward every device on this interface. Other devices are not forwarded.
forwarding.destinationsHelp: Optional. Leave empty to forward all internet traffic of these devices.
forwarding.egressTProxyHelp: Intercepts TCP and UDP of these devices into a TProxy inbound on this host instead of routing it.
forwarding.noTProxy: No TProxy inbound exists. Create one in Inbounds first.
forwarding.masqueradeHelp: Replaces the devices' addresses with this host's address on the way out. Needed when the next router does not know how to reach your LAN. Off by default.
forwarding.egressRoutesHelp: Forwards through the normal routing table, which already includes your route rules.
forwarding.noSourceFilter: On this platform every device on the LAN interface is forwarded; limiting it to some devices is not available.

platform.darwin: macOS: forwarding uses PF through Yuhaiin's own anchor (com.apple/yuhaiin). Your pf.conf and other anchors are not changed. TProxy interception is not available.
platform.windows: Windows: forwarding is turned on per interface and follows the routing table, including your route rules. Limiting it to some devices, choosing an egress per rule and NAT are not available.

interfaces.title: Interfaces
interfaces.help: Interfaces present on this host right now. Yuhaiin never deletes or reconfigures interfaces it does not own.

ownershipHelp.external: A tunnel created by another program, such as WireGuard or Tailscale.

interfaces.missingHelp: These interfaces or TUNs are used by rules but do not exist now. Their rules are paused and resume automatically.
interfaces.viaTun: Choose it as a Yuhaiin TUN in route rules.

routes.title: System routes
routes.help: The routing table the operating system uses right now. Routes Yuhaiin installed are marked with the rule they come from; everything else belongs to the system or other programs and is never changed.

sourceHelp.required: Keeps a Yuhaiin TUN working, such as its subnet or a FakeIP pool.
sourceHelp.vpn: Passed to the Android VPN for a route rule.
sourceHelp.stale: Marked as Yuhaiin's but not part of the current configuration. It is removed on the next start.

routes.rulesHelp: Linux policy rules decide which table a packet looks up, in priority order.
routes.androidNote: Android does not let apps read the kernel routing table. These are the routes Android reports for each network; Yuhaiin's VPN routes are marked.
routes.androidVpnOnly: This app version cannot read Android's network routes. Only the routes passed to the Yuhaiin VPN are shown.
